# scripts/mutation-pr.sh under the real timeout (or gtimeout): a gremlins run that passes MUTATION_TIMEOUT fails with its own line.
# Only gremlins is a stub. It sleeps for longer than the limit, so the limiter stops it.
[!exec:jq] skip
[!exec:git] skip
[!exec:timeout] [!exec:gtimeout] skip
env HOME=$WORK/home
env GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null
env GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
chmod 755 fake/gremlins
env PATH=$WORK/fake:$PATH

exec git init -q -b main repo
cp a.go repo/a.go
cp gomod repo/go.mod
script mutation-pr.sh repo/scripts/mutation-pr.sh
script mutation-exec.sh repo/scripts/mutation-exec.sh
chmod 755 repo/scripts/mutation-exec.sh
exec git -C repo add a.go go.mod scripts
exec git -C repo -c user.name=e2e -c user.email=e2e@example.com commit -q -m base
exec git -C repo checkout -q -b change
cp a2.go repo/a.go
exec git -C repo add a.go
exec git -C repo -c user.name=e2e -c user.email=e2e@example.com commit -q -m change

# The limit is 1 second and gremlins sleeps for 30. The run is a tool error: exit code 1, no counts line and no end marker.
# The limit starts before the stub starts. The first exec of a freshly written executable file can take over 1 second
# (1.58 s measured on a Mac), so the limit can stop the stub before its first line. The script asserts nothing about
# the stub's own output.
env MUTATION_TIMEOUT=1
exitcode 1 sh repo/scripts/mutation-pr.sh main
stdout '^mutation-pr: the run exceeded MUTATION_TIMEOUT=1s$'
! stdout '^mutation-pr: applied='
! stdout '^mutation-pr: end '

-- gomod --
module example.com/r

go 1.27
-- a.go --
package a
-- a2.go --
package a

func F(x int) bool { return x > 0 }
-- fake/gremlins --
#!/bin/sh
exec sleep 30
